specAnchors.text: understand that mutation is a rare, random change in genetic material that can be inherited

primer.text: Short but load-bearing: the core definition of mutation, a rare and random alteration of the genetic material that offspring can receive, plus the two qualifiers exams attach to it — changes happen continuously, and most of them leave the protein effectively unchanged.

modules.title: The Core Definition
modules.opening: A mutation is a rare, random change in the base sequence of a gene or chromosome; it can be inherited, it happens continuously across generations, and most of the time the protein it codes for stays effectively unchanged.
keyPoints: Mutations are rare, random changes in genetic material.
They occur in the DNA base sequence of a gene or a chromosome.
Mutations can be inherited by offspring.
They happen continuously rather than in bursts.
In most cases the protein is untouched, or nudged so slightly that its function survives.

low.restatement: A mutation is a rare random DNA change, inheritable and mostly harmless.
low.analogy: An occasional wrong keystroke in a long manuscript that rarely spoils the story.
low.examPointer: Hit all four qualifiers: rare, random, inheritable, continuous.

medium.restatement: The base sequence dictates the amino acid sequence, so the protein changes only when the mutation reaches that far.
medium.analogy: A recipe change only matters if it alters an ingredient that the dish actually uses.
medium.examPointer: Pair this definition with the advanced note's effect ladder.

glossary.definition: A rare and random alteration of the genetic material, which offspring can receive.
The order of bases along a gene or chromosome.
To receive genetic material from a parent.
